items.statement: Plain words: every non-geometry decision (building needs of a 6 000-person town, relative house sizes by wealth, trade affinities, neighbourhood names, thieves' guild fronts, wall materials) is read from a table; V11 is the book of every table: columns, units, readers, row sources, and the rows that are design choices (building ladder shack to cathedral, district kinds, named quarters, translation of SettlementForge's 280 institution kinds, covers, sectors, the owner's siting rulebook of 2026-09-28).

Plain words: one-click map unchanged; tables editor shows plain rows with per-cell provenance (reference emulated, own judgment, owner, corpus later); changing a cell changes exactly the map parts that read it, as an undoable edit; the clerk names the rows that pulled a building to its site.

Plain words: the siting rulebook is factored: each kind carries a profile (emits smell/smoke/noise/fire risk/fouled water/heavy traffic/crowds/disorder/sacredness; cannot bear; needs running water/road/gate/harbour/market/space/safety/secrecy; customers street/town/travellers/rich/underworld; buys/sells; law and sacred side; clusters or spreads) and a dozen general rules turn profiles into soft pulls; a few dozen named pairs (dyers upstream of tanners); only true physical needs are hard (watermill on water); owner's 'a correlating general rule'.

Plain words: SettlementForge custom content lands sensibly via scene archetype, category, tags and name words mapped to profiles; its supply chain placed as one connected thing (raw material at river/quarry, processors inward, seller by market).

Plain words (item 109): underground numbers: ruins of an older civilisation certain where the dossier names ancient ruins or a ruined landmark, possible anywhere once fantasy setting on; four ancient street plans; which ruin parts last longest; break-in chances of cellar/well/mine into cave or ruin; depth for a void to stay secret under a great city; burial rule J111 (~20:05): churches get crypts (cathedral always, the largest), catacombs only under cemeteries (and in a city/metropolis under a worked-out quarry ossuary); town at most one catacomb, city more by number of churches; each grows about a tenth a decade at most, never shrinks.

Plain words (item 110): numbers for terraces (slope and step height thresholds; wall material by ground wealth), raised roads on arches over ravines / between high quarters and aqueducts when wells fall short in city or metropolis only (town only when user draws), stepped tiers by culture (rare), small buildings on bridge/pier/mole/quay with trade limits (never forge, never cathedral), fort/lighthouse/watchtower at a mole head; every row user-changeable; all switched off = map exactly as before.
V11 does not hold name vocabularies (grammars and authoring only), palette colours (base §8.2), or rows other volumes own (cited, never copied).

Ladder step types (dossier.ladders; item 108): source ladder and subsumption are SF's own pairs as g quotes them (provenance sf:institutionLadders.js@5d699cc68, BCR-V11-21, owner's own program); inferred pairs read from the catalogue's tier names and re-checked by V08 against the ladder file when the port reads it (V08 §3.5; a disagreement is a table fix, reported); an unnumbered COUNT, QUARTER or GUILD record's member range = range column = value at kind's lowest tier; rungScale multiplies it only above that tier ({CITY 2, METROPOLIS 3} TOWN kind, {METROPOLIS 1.5} CITY kind, none METROPOLIS kind; multiple_court_buildings (M) yields 4-10 at METROPOLIS, never 16-40); at a village rung an unnumbered record takes V07 §2.4's range row (village.json rules.ladders.ranges) by V08 §3.5.1 (b) (keyed by step type and the class playing the member class; J-V7.105) else this range unscaled; every member count is S2's per-capita count clamped into the range (108 (b)); a numbered record's own range wins.

A COUNT whose member is a pin (@pin:<kind>) sets a floor only: members = max(range low end, the pin's own coverage count at the rung: V07 §3.10 well rows at village rungs, §4.7 furniture step at base rungs), never clamped to the range top (J-V11.61); SIZE's factor multiplies template footprint and plot budget, sigma's rank and, for a crypted class, cryptM2; identity names the QuarterIdentityRow a QUARTER record claims (T-V11-2); rows never calibrated (range, rungScale, sizeFactor, inferred rows included, §13.9 (7)); a change is a table fix reviewed with V08.

Step semantics: a kind absent from the table is no step; a COUNT's members keyed #k (J-A74.73); a QUARTER record owns its district's members of the class and, by the class's ordinary spread (item 107), members outside it; a GUILD record is one guildhall plus a collective of the trade's members tied to it, its hall bound into a guild COUNT record of the same dossier by V08 §3.5.1 (c) family rule (J-V8.83), never a further hall (108 (c)); SIZE is one building; REPLACEMENT keeps only the greater (108 (a)); no double counting (108 (c)); cemetery_network members are burial faces (V04 §3.5.1 candidates; at METROPOLIS the first in the catacomb order, §3.23.8).

Burial ladder across 1 500 people: burial_ground (T, H) -> graveyard (V) -> parish_burial_grounds (W, a COUNT of church plots' churchyards) -> burial_grounds_and_charnel_house (C, SIZE); a tier change is never a closure: V08 §2.6a (4) re-binds the lesser's face to the greater's key (churchyard keeps lineage and opening year, which V07 §3.12 step 6 carries across the hand-off); no churchyard bound to two records.

V08's re-check against the ladder file (V08 §3.5.1 (f), V08 §13 X1) applied: file rows are ladder or subsumption; hospital_network's and dungeon_delving_supply_district's lessers are the file's; file pairs added as rows (parish_church, multiple_water_sources, theaters, wizard_s_tower, mages_guild, caravan_masters_exchange, major_hospital's almshouse); rows the file lacks but dossiers carry in both forms stay inferred (108 (c) must merge them). Plain words: V12 sets the rule tables' numbers right and proves it against other generators (MFCG, FTG, Neighbourhood, Village Generator, Fantasy Manor) and later the owner's historical map collection, never changing how the generator works; four loops: (1) measuring references on towns whose seeds were fixed by formula before capture; only numbers cross into the product folder; (2) measuring ours with the very same code; every number has a band by one rule; nightly report 'in band', 'out of band', 'for information'; (3) tuning: a table value changed (never code) by a recorded search on practice towns, checked on a held-out set; each change a new table version declared in release notes; saved towns open exactly as made; (4) the owner's eye: sitting page at each big milestone, pairs ours vs reference, sides hidden, three questions per pair (easier to read, more like a real town, rather use), about 35-45 minutes, can be split; only the owner's answers let a milestone say 'at parity' or 'mastered'.

Plain words: tendencies not guarantees: the harness proves each leaning by counting over many practice towns (rank vs the same town shuffled at random, ties broken by a fair coin; counting members exactly; watching a rate climb as towns grow), rules worked out beforehand so chance almost never passes and a real leaning almost always does; a failing bar re-runs once on fresh towns before anything changes; where the owner's volume states how a bar passes, that wins. Owner's rules stay the owner's (catacomb only under a cemetery, cathedral always crypted, raised ways only in cities): no tuning, fallback or historical map moves them; a historical counter-example goes to the owner as a question with 'keep the rule'; catacombs checked never to shrink on every rebuild (epoch, regeneration, re-derive, New random, upgrade) and to fill ossuaries when they cannot grow.

Plain words: later the historical maps adjust default numbers and bands, never machinery; one historical example proves possible, never common; only a fair pre-chosen sample of measured plans says how common; collection teaches drawing, never naming; its 53 held-back plates never used; MFCG and FTG behaviour stays exactly reachable through the parity presets; historical values arrive as a 'historical' layer and the owner decides at a before-and-after sitting whether it becomes default. items.statement: The dossier: calibration never targets a dossier fact: tables/dossier/* never a calibration target (§13.9 (7)); B-DOSSIER-lite fixtures are not a seed family of any calibration run (a SettlementForge fixture never moves a default); FTG pairs take populations from the captures (§13.6 (2)), never a dossier; calibration always guards the dossier fixtures (§3.7.4: B-DOSSIER-lite on every accepted candidate); bars read dossier fields as fixture inputs through derivation rows (V08 traces; derived fixtures registered in §13.2's frozen fixture manifest and item 84, §17.1 (3) the one door).

Dossier fields read as fixture inputs: population (DR23, DR7) -> item 108 (f) population sweep levels (x0.5 .. x2) as derived fixtures <dossier>@pop×k; a level leaving [1 500, 120 000] skipped, reported notApplicable, never a failure; site.ruinEvidence (DR-V8.2) -> a level's forced ruin source (109 (b)) as a fixture record, never a test-only branch (J-V12.35); terrain and mining deposits (DR-V8.3, DR1) -> mining boost's higherWith strata (109 (a)); economy.chains (activeChains, DR-V8.5) -> 104 (h)(8) and 105 custom-chain levels (V08 fixtures); burial, church, cathedral, monastery records, Cemetery network (DR-V8.4, DR9) -> catacomb count and crypt levels (109 (k)); wealth.label (DR6 -> intent.wealthLevel) -> elevated-road prosperity trend dossier arm (110 (b)); institutions of significance >= 20 and custom landmark records on high ground (DR-V8.8) -> elevated-road landmark higherWith; water-system record aqueduct_or_water_system (DR-V8.7, V11 mapping to conduit_house) -> raised bump shift records name B-DOSSIER-lite towns carrying it; read never targeted: at CITY and METROPOLIS makes the aqueduct need count as met (V11 §3.24.7 (3)); no raised way has a dossier source.

Data model scope: everything test-side or repository data (code and JSON in @plat/testkit and plat/calibration/, research-side files never entering plat/) except the two optional provenance fields of §2.10 (evidence ids, ownerRule stamp) riding in shipped tables and dist/evidence.json; none is document state: a .plat document holds the table versions they produced (§6.4). Units m, m2, ha, deg, share [0,1], count, perHa, perKm, ratio, bits, ms, s, luma (8-bit Rec. 601), rb (8-bit R - B), chroma (CIELAB C*ab), z (standard scores), none.

MetricId (dotted, stable, never reused: 'street.turn100', 'lots.r4.60', 'fg.coverWalled', 'fm.towers'); MetricInput geo (on a MeasureInput, same code on reference, corpus map and ours)  /  model (only our model: plots, prosperity, generation report, core statistics record §13.2)  /  render (PNG: §8.2 measurement render, city band at matched scale §8.5)  /  timing (§12.1 timing phase normalised by calibration score)  /  trace (a stage's recorded trace at bench level: S8 cut log, S10b placement log)  /  counts (integer counts a harness writes: FM family and element counts, NG hood and VG village counts); Unit union as §2.

MetricDef {id, version (semver: major definition changed, every baseline re-measured §3.4.3; minor new field; patch no value change), input, scale metric / free (free: angles, shares, counts, ratios, rank statistics, valid on relative-scale input), sign positive / any (band widening multiplicative vs additive §3.5.2), absFloor (smallest band half-width), requires FeatureKind[] (lacking one -> notApplicable, never 0), stages StageIds (a tuning run may only move cells those stages read §3.7.2), output scalar / distribution (fixed bin edges) / vector, perSeed median / mean / share / value / sample, row (the §13.5/§13.7/volume row it serves), tolerance {abs?, rel?} (two implementations agree, T-V12-3), costMs per CITY town single thread (§6), sampling? {label, n} (R4's 1 500 buildings), plain (release-note sentence with {ours}, {band}, {dir} slots)}.

Metric code is pure: no clock, no global state; transcendental functions from dmath (§17.4); every sampling metric draws from its testkit stream (§3.13), so one MeasureInput gives bit-identical values on every host (J-V12.9); every verdict-deciding field (sign, absFloor, output.edges, tolerance, costMs, stages) filled for every catalogue row, explicitly or by §3.4.2's default rules; a row whose field neither states nor defaults fails plat build.

Two generated metric families (J-V12.65): bar.<barId> = verdict statistic of one registered owner bar (<barId> verbatim: bar.T-V6-8, bar.T-V2-32, bar.T16-4, bar.T110b.viaduct); resolves to registrations whose id or ownerBar equals <barId> (several: vector of statistics, passes only when each passes): StatBarSpec (StatBarResult.statistic), NullModelSpec (the statistic its pass rule tests: share of towns with u > 0.5 on the rank route, pooled p on pooled route, median margin on margin route, own p in a holm family; siting.<spec> stays the placement statistic), or BenchBarDef (for every bar a register line names that no spec carries, e.g. V06 T-V6-37 beside V04 T-V4-45); unit, stages, row the registration's; input model, scale free, sign any, perSeed value, scalar (vector for several clauses); no band (verdict is the bar's own pass rule); costMs 0; plat parity writes one row per registered bar of its tier (metric bar.<barId>, statistic as ours, bar's verdict, baselineIds empty); a <barId> with no registration does not exist (lint fails an entry naming it).

frame.<table>.<column>: a declared sample frame's value for one calibratable column (table id matched as the longest registered TableId prefix): target rows (§3.10.2) of the geo metrics the corpus run touching that column's cells targets (§3.10.5), each read in the frame's corpus variant, report row the frame's A2 verdict under its pack (§3.10.6); notApplicable before M-CAL (read at M-CAL and each later corpus run M-CAL/<layer>, §3.10.1), on every source but a frame, and for a column no frame's run targets (its corpus entry then closes fixed with 'no admissible frame'); exists for every calibratable column.

PresetArm = 'default'  /  PresetId (J-V12.72): 'default' = recipe with no parity preset (§3.5 O and C rows; an owner bar's own towns); else a registered preset PresetId (V11 §2.2: MFCG / FTG / VG / FM / NG); every preset field of §2's records is a PresetArm except CalibrationRun.layer and CalibrationEntry.target, which name a preset ENTRY of a cell (FM / VG / NG), never an arm.

BenchBarDef (@plat/testkit/bars; an owner's bar that is neither NullModelSpec nor StatBarSpec, registered in code by its owner once a register entry names it as bar.<id>, X-V12-15): id (owner's bar id verbatim 'T-V6-8', 'T-V2-32', 'T16-4', 'T-V11-30'), owner base / V01..V12, statistic {what (owner's plain words), unit}, stages (StageIds, V06's phase ids for a history bar; §3.7.2 (4) reads them), towns {family ('bcity', 'golden' or owner fixture family e.g. V06 H-100), perSetting, settings [{rung, water, preset PresetArm ('default' for a bar's own towns)}]}, tier pr / nightly / milestone, run(towns [{seed, doc, bench: stats(doc, {level: 'bench'})}]) -> {statistic number / number[] (one per clause in owner's order), verdict pass / fail / notApplicable} (pure).

ReferenceId = MFCG / FTG / NG / VG / FM (Dwellings stays a research-side note, V03 §7, never a source); FeatureKind = way / block / plot / building / wall / tower / gate / castle / square / district / water / river / pier / green / field / tree / closure / enclosure (item 106: natural edge closing a circuit LineString; enclosed area Polygon) / gallery / chamber (underground profile only) / retaining (110 (a), never a wall) / raisedSupport (110 (b) pier or abutment footprint, never a building) / span (110 (b), f item 447; read by no metric); an aqueduct has no kind of its own: a way of class aqueduct, raisedKind aqueduct (f 447).

MeasureInput {header {source PLAT / ReferenceId / corpus, build, scale metric / relative (no metric scale: NG vertex captures, a plate without a scale bar), unitM?, centre (plaza, else wall ring centroid, else building centroid), rung?, population?, water?, seedLabel? (never a place name), layer? surface / underground (underground only for our towns), frame?, options? (numbers and flags only)}, features MeasureFeature[]}; MeasureFeature {kind, id (opaque, file-local), geometry (GeoJSON, rings closed on read), props {class? (way arterial / street / lane / alley / track / aqueduct / unknown; wall curtain / castle; water sea / river / lake; square plaza / market / other; building a V11 §3.4 family key or unknown; gate land / water; closure J-VI.3's six kinds shore / cliff / gorge / marsh / sheer / enceinte (f 447); gallery and chamber UndergroundSystem.kind with 'ruin', fissure variant 'cavern'), state? (closure state or 'unexcavated' 109 (j)(2)), widthM?, storeys?, heightM?, district?, use? (V11 family key), prosperity? (PLAT only, 3 decimals), part? (0 ground, >= 1 raised arena part), raisedKind?, source? generated / declared (derived at read, f 244 ST-06; dossier declares no arches), reason? drop / link / water, onDeck? mole / pier / quay / bridge, stair?, ramp?, stepMinCm?, stepMaxCm?}}.

Our way classes in the profile: measureInputOf maps §2 WayClass once: through, primary -> arterial; secondary -> street; lane, cul_de_sac -> lane; alley -> alley; track, path -> track; bridge and ford take the class of the way they carry; quay and pier not ways for these metrics (pier features stay); aqueduct stays aqueduct, in no traffic class (no way graph, no way-distance statistic); a reference adapter maps its own classes (§3.2.2); unmappable class unknown, read by no class-specific metric.

MeasureInput carries no name, label text, colour or style (J-V12.2); for our towns measureInputOf(doc, opts) builds it from the model; T-V12-4 holds it equal to the metric GeoJSON export read back (use, district, prosperity included, BCR-V12-15; item 110 kinds and properties BCR-V12-17 as f 447, IN-V12-4); one reading rule: the reader drops every exported property the profile does not declare: deckMinCm, deckMaxCm, underuseSince on a raised way; way, key, state on a support; use and state on a span; wall, run, highSide, material, state on a retaining wall; condition on a wall (f 575); deck and tiers on a plot or building; model-side builder never writes them; no geo metric reads them (raised.*, retaining.*, tier.* are model metrics reading records).

Runs merged on read (J-V12.68): f 447 exports a retaining wall as one LineString per run of equal state; f 575 splits §11.1 wall LineStrings per run of equal condition; the reader merges them before any metric: retaining features with one wall id become one feature joined in run order (closed wall ring closed), stepMinCm/stepMaxCm least and greatest over runs; wall features of one enceinte's id joining end to end become one feature per built stretch (a maximal part of the trace between closure edges, in trace order), each keeping its entity id; wall, run, state, condition then dropped; a breached, dismantled or landfall-buried stretch measures as the built stretch it is part of; a run boundary is never a stretch end; measureInputOf writes the same (T-V12-4 holds on towns whose walls a decline, landfall or hand edit struck).

Item 110 entities in the profile (J-V12.62): a raised way's ways carry part >= 1 with raisedKind, source, reason; an aqueduct is its way (class aqueduct, raisedKind aqueduct); supports raisedSupport polygons, spans span polygons; a retaining wall one retaining line (runs merged) with stepMinCm, stepMaxCm; way segments crossing it carry stair or ramp; deck buildings are building features with onDeck; a stepped building's heightM is the top of its stack (V02 heights envelope); no founding rung rides in the profile: raised.generatedBelowCity is a model metric reading the founding epoch's record (f 244 stores none, ST-06).

Enclosure (item 106): a wall metric reads the outermost enclosure: the enclosure polygon where the source gives one (ours from the export of an enceinte closed by ring, shore or barrier, BCR-V12-15; a corpus plan's drawn circuit), else the outermost wall ring of class curtain; wall features are built stretches only (one per built stretch after merging f 575's condition runs); closure features are natural edges closing the circuit (106 (a)), never counted as wall length, tower stretches or gates; the MFCG adapter splits its exported city ring the same way (§3.2.2).

Underground profile (item 109): undergroundInputOf(doc, systemId) writes one underground system: galleries as gallery LineStrings with widths, chambers as chamber Polygons, each with system kind and state, every part in every state (a ruin's collapsed and filled parts included, plan measured as laid), header.layer underground, options.sharedAxis when a ruin took 109 (c)'s shared-axis chance, header.centre at system centroid; exists only for our towns, never crosses the firewall; a chamber's monument (V04 Chamber.monument, 110 (c)) is written as building features of the underground layer with props.class the monument's row; no plan metric (plan.*, ruin.blockArea, grid.*) reads a building of that layer (T-V12-33).

BaselinesFile (plat/packages/testkit/baselines/baselines.json; the one file the parity CLI reads §13.5): schema 'plat.baselines/2', metricsVersion, pins ReferencePin[] {reference, build, since milestone}, rows Baseline[] (append-only: superseded never deleted), crossings CrossingRecord[] {date, seat, checker, added, superseded, checks [{id C1..C10, pass true}], scanVersion, fileHash}. Baseline gains (BCR-V12-1): reference ReferenceId  /  corpus:frame:<s>  /  corpus:map:<s> (FM added; corpus ids salted), metricVersion, supersedes?, sample {family, indices? [0, n] (always from 0), captures?, failed? [{index, reason}] (listed, never silently skipped)}, estimator single / minmax / type7, spreadKS? {p90, pairs}, scale metric / free, evidence?, frameN? (corpus rows); ftg-captures.json, ng-counts.json and §13.6 (9) panel files cross by the same check; FM counts and VG counts are ordinary Baseline rows of input counts.

SeedFamily {label, reduce u32 / parkMiller (1 + (H32 mod 2 147 483 646), MINSTD range, §13.6 (2)), priority 0 gate .. 5 null and sweep}; seedOf(family, path) = reduce(H32(label + '/' + path.join('/'))); a seed equal to one in the COLLISION DOMAIN gains '/r1', '/r2' ... (J-V12.4); domain = every higher-priority family's FULL declared count (bref 100, golden 12, known 1 per fixture, bcity 1 000 per setting) compared per (rung, water) where the path carries them and globally where not (sweep, known); capture families excluded; never depends on what a tier has drawn; §13.6 formulas unchanged.

Seed families (label / reduce / priority / count / consumer / check vector): bref/<ref>/<rung>/<water>/<i> u32 0, nightly 20 milestone 100, our side of every parity row, bref/MFCG/TOWN/none/0 -> 1738244370; golden/<rung>/<water>/<i> u32 1, 12, golden suite (§13.3; BCR-V12-7), golden/CITY/river/11 -> 639553850; known/<id> u32 1, 1 per fixture, known-city fixtures, known/K1 -> 3403473561, known/K2 -> 3205843448; bcity/<rung>/<water>/<i> u32 2, 1 000 (B-CITY-lite i < 50), B-CITY (§13.2; BCR-V12-7), bcity/TOWN/none/0 -> 104466889; capture/<ref>/<size or template>/<options>/<i> parkMiller (MFCG, NG, VG) else u32, 3, MFCG 10 per matched size, NG 5 per template, VG per V07, capture/MFCG/40/plain/0 -> 2003595629; tune/<run>/train / holdout/<rung>/<water>/<i> and .../guard/TOWN/<water>/<i> u32 4, 30 each, tune/2026-09-28-example/train/CITY/none/0 -> 1236353098, .../guard/TOWN/none/0 -> 2478365614; null/<spec>/<rung>/<water>/<i> and confirmation .../c1/<i> u32 5, 50 and c1 100, null/T71-3/CITY/none/0 -> 1233256533, .../c1/0 -> 338389334, null/T110b.viaduct/CITY/none/0 -> 4261915227; sweep/<spec>/<level>/<i> (exactMonotone: sweep/<spec>/any/<i>) u32 5, per rule, sweep/T109-a.relief/mountainous/0 -> 4027728537, sweep/T109-j5.access/TOWN/0 -> 649597841, sweep/T109k6.extent/any/0 -> 1148414874, sweep/T110b.elevated.prosperity/w0.1/0 -> 4196945930; d5 families (§13.6 (2)), d5-fm/<panel>/<i>, d5-vg/<panel>/<rung>/<tags>/<i>, d5/M-CAL/<rung>/<water>/<i> (later d5/M-CAL/<layer>/...), d5/M-CAL/TOWN/none/0 -> 1899492655.

A family is prefix-stable (first n seeds never change when a tier draws more): B-CITY-lite is B-CITY's prefix; nightly bref seeds are the milestone's first twenty; pooled siting bars stated on '>= 200 B-CITY seeds per rung' read B-CITY's nightly towns and pay only for permutations (J-V12.40); null/ families remain for settings B-CITY lacks; check vectors in docs/validation/bench/v12_rev_h32.out (script v12_h32_vectors.py).

CellRef {table, rowKey, column, band?}; CalibrationRun (BCR-V12-3; plat/calibration/runs/<id>.json): id 'cal/<milestone>/<slug>/<n>' fixed before the run (salts train and holdout families); kind reference / fallback / corpus; source {reference, build} / {fallback register entry id} / {corpus {adapter, version, frames, maps}}; cells [{ref, lo, hi, step, from (lo, hi inside the column's range and at or above an owner-stamped calibration minimum §3.7.2 (5)), layer inPlace / {pack 'historical:<frame>'} / {preset FM / VG / NG} (the cell's preset entry a register entry names: a reference run vs that preset's reference, or a fallback run applying that entry's fallback; J-V12.63, J-V12.67)}]; objective {targets [{metric, rung / building / hood / village, preset PresetArm, baselineIds, weight}], guards GuardSet}; search; seeds {perSetting 30, settings [{rung, water, population, preset}]}; budgetCpuH default 2, hard stop; evaluations [{values, score, guardFlips, report}]; chosen; holdout; status accepted / rejected / fallback-applied / aborted-budget / refused; refusal? {cell, rule}; changes [{ref, from, to, evidence}]; before, after; shifts (ShiftRecord ids cause calibration); date; seat.

SearchSpec grid (values <= 16 candidates)  /  golden (one cell, maxIter <= 12)  /  coordinate (rounds <= 3, maxIterPerCell <= 8, <= 4 cells); GuardSet {parityRows 'allPassing', cBars true, ownerRuleBars true, frozen (entries that must not move), fixtureSuites (B-DOSSIER-lite / ownerRuleHooks / K1 / K2; run once on the chosen candidate before the holdout decision §3.7.5), townGuard (true when any cell is a raised-way row: 30 TOWN towns on tune/<id>/guard/TOWN join the guard evaluation §3.7.4)}.

CalibrationEntry (plat/calibration/register.json; one per provisional number): id 'cal.<table>.<rowKey>.<column>' / 'thr.<letter>' / 'band.<metric>.<rung>' (preset entry adds '@FM', '@VG' or '@NG'); target {cell, preset?} / {threshold §13.7 letter} / {band {metric, rung}} / {column {table, column, rows? glob, preset?}} (preset: the entry is that preset's entry, never its default; no '@NG' id exists until a volume states one, V01 §3.15, J-V1.98); owner base / V01..V12; metric MetricId[] (catalogue ids or members of siting.<spec>, bar.<barId>, frame.<table>.<column>); method measure / tune / panel / corpus (measure: confirmed by its metrics at due milestone exit; tune: set by a reference run vs the entry's own reference when due (item 34 cells at M0, V02 §3.10.8 FM entries at M6c, V07 rules.race.densityPower@VG at V-M4), accepted run's value its confirmation, a rejected run applying the fallback; where the owning volume states it (V07 §3.15) the run opens only when the metric misses its band, else confirmed with a history row; panel: a rated pass; corpus: corpus stage at M-CAL or later M-CAL/<layer> for columns first landed after M-CAL); due (milestone; corpus due a CorpusRunId); fallback {mechanism, notAchieved}; status provisional / confirmed / fallback-applied / not-achieved / owner-set / fixed; line? 'default'; panel? {id, group?, question legibility / realism / charm / reads}; stages? [{method, due, panel?, metric?, possibility?}] (staged entry: method/due/panel hold the current stage's); history [{date, value, run?, panel?, milestone?, cells?, stage? {index, outcome pass / fail / unrated}, held?}].

History cells flag: cells: true marks a cells row whose value is the target's compiled cells by row key: --defaults' first row, a named entry's first row (written with the target's compiled cells, a preset entry's excepted), moved-value and rows-added rows (§3.11), a later line's restating row, a pick's row whose release moves the target's cells in place (§3.9: next table version, declared shift), a run's row that changed the target in place (§3.7.6 step 5); absent on a metrics row (milestone exit readings, corpus frame.* reading), a panel's row, a pick's row moving no cell, a held or status row, a pack or preset run's row.

One knob, one entry, one column: the register check fails when two entries, or two compiled columns, name one mechanism under different names (a cell's default and its FM, VG or NG entry are two knobs told apart by preset); the J111 fold's kept columns are V04's CatacombRule.cryptJoin and CatacombRule.growthCapShare (read per year over the span, V06 J-V6.53). A panel entry is confirmed by a rated pass of its panel on its question; while unrated it stays provisional and its exit row reads 'provisional - not rated': never fails an exit, never lets its gate be claimed (§13.6 (7)).

ClassSelector {classes?, families?, tags?} (V11 §2.3 keys); StatSpec: meanDistTo {to ClassSelector / market / gate / quay / water / wall, agg? mean / median} (metres along the way graph); shareWithin {to, radiusM} (pooled route); servedShare {unit? coverage / district} (share of the subject class's coverage units holding >= 1 member, each unit as V11 §2.3 defines at a plot; coverage default reads compiled profile.coverage; district forces districts of >= 30 households (105 (k)); one class per spec; null scope town only); nnSameKind (median nearest same-class distance; town only); downstreamShare, downwindShare (pooled); prestigeShare (item 71, T71-3; pooled); flowOrder {chain} (104 (h)(8)); chainSpread {chain?} (104 (g): mean way distance between a chain instance's in-town nodes); meanDistToPartners {role dominantOutputConsumers / providers / inputs / demand} (105 (k)).

NullPass: rank {townShare 0.70, medianU 0.60} (default except pooled statistics)  /  pooledExact {alpha 0.01, minShift?} (shareWithin, downstreamShare, downwindShare, prestigeShare)  /  margin {value: median over towns of S_obs - mean S_k (T71-3's 0.15)}  /  holm {family, alpha 0.01} (owner's clauses Holm-corrected, V11 T-V11-12). NullModelSpec {id ('T71-3', 'T103-e.tannery-downstream', 'T105-k.shared-provider'), owner, ownerBar? (its statement wins, J-V12.48), subject, statistic, null {scope block / district / town, eligible hardNeeds / sameSizeClass / anyPlot, permutations K = 20}, expect lower / higher, pass (default pooledExact for member-on-plot shares, rank otherwise, J-V12.12), towns {source bcity, perRung 200 when owner says so else 50} / {source null, perSetting 50}, seeds {settings [{rung, water, preset}]}, applies {requires? river / coast / walls / customChain / islands, minMembers default 1 pooled, 3 rank}, variant? {distance way / euclid, eligible, subjects plots / buildingsWithUse} (corpus comparisons only)}. NullModelResult {spec, setting, towns, skipped, share (towns with u > 0.5), medianU, pooled? {observed, nullMean, p}, verdict pass / suspect / fail / insufficient, confirmation?, perSeed [{seed, obs, nullMean, lt, eq, u}]}.

Registration refuses: a servedShare or nnSameKind spec at a scope other than town (district or block permutation conserves them); a servedShare spec whose subject is not exactly one class (per coverage class: one spec per class, id <bar>.<class>), whose class has no coverage row under unit coverage, or whose class's unit is settlement (T-V11-13's roster clause, reported notApplicable); a pooled-route spec whose pooled null share over its first 50 towns exceeds 0.85 (below 0.02 for expect lower) - the headroom lint (executed: power <= 0.09 at a 0.3 pull, critique_v12_pooled_exact.out); owner restates the indicator or states its complement.

Indicator (one yes/no per instance, from bench statistics and explain link list): flowOrder (104 (h)(8)); withinComfort (104 (h)(8), 107 (g): link way distance <= good's comfortM); voidAccessible (109 (j)(3),(3b): cavern or ruin system with an access point, direct or via linked systems); voidSealedDeep (109 (j)(5): per DEEP VOID - a connected component of a cavern or ruin system's parts whose tops lie deeper than DigRule.reachM below every footprint over them - sealed when no access reaches it); ruinChosen (109 (i): undercity's first void source a ruin, among undercities where ruin and cavern both qualify); present {system cavern / ruin} (109 (a), (j)(1)); raised {raisedKind, source generated} (110 (b)). Quantity ladder.members / catacomb.extentM2 / catacomb.fill / catacomb.growthM2; Step epoch / regenerate / {rederive StageId} / {newRandom 'system'} / upgradeReplay / {dossierEvent} / extendGrowth; Level {id, rung, water, preset, site?, dossier? (manifest fixture id incl. <dossier>@pop×k), intent? {wealthLevel}, populationScale?, epochs?, requires? (volume whose generator the level needs: notApplicable until landed)}.

PairedMeasure (ruin's laid plan vs town above within its outline, per seed): metric ruin.blockArea / grid.r4 / grid.axis; differs logRatio atLeast ln 1.5  /  absDiff atLeast 0.15  /  axisDeg atLeast 10 skipWhen sharedAxis. (stated parameters win, J-V12.48), rule, levels (ordered for trend and exactMonotone; strata for higherWith; pooled settings otherwise), seeds {perLevel, max (steps of 50 up to max until minimum met)}, stopAfter? Adapters (research/baselines/adapters/<ref>.py -> inputs/<ref>/<build>/<capture>.metric.geojson): MFCG: JSON export in metres; each exported road a way of class arterial; each footprint and prism a building of class unknown; first wall polygon the city's enclosure and curtain, second the castle curtain and a castle feature; gates are city ring vertices touching a road vertex less those shared with the castle ring (class land); district, square, green, field polygons, river centrelines (with river width), pier segments, sea polygon mapped; shore split (106): ring edges whose two vertices lie on the sea polygon boundary within 0.5 m become closure features class shore, rest stays curtain, ring stays enclosure; ring vertex on a river centreline is a gate of class water; towers are castle ring non-gate vertices plus city ring vertices neither gate, castle-shared, nor inside a shore closure; lanes not exported (lane metrics read the derived street graph §3.4.1). FTG: road graph main -> arterial, district -> street, suburb -> lane; footprints; wall chains and tower points; fields; water outlines; cm to m; no plots (item 49). NG: blocks, lots, buildings from vertex captures, relative; bent-cut signature values are §13.5's recorded measurements entered as trace rows. VG: V07 §7 features; FM: counts file.

Measuring with one implementation: at M-1 seats measure with research-side scripts written from §3.4's definitions (red-team scripts of docs/validation/bench/README.md as starting point); from M1 plat measure is the one implementation: research re-runs every baseline through the released CLI on the same MeasureInput files; T-V12-3 holds the two within each metric's tolerance; where they differ, the seat finds the wrong definition and the product's value replaces the M-1 row as a superseding row with a declared baselineShift (§13.3) naming the metric (J-V12.1); a render metric (recoverability) keeps §16 M-1's cross-check within 0.01 on M1's golden renders; T-V12-3 and T-V12-6 read captures so are research-side checks (check_t3.py, check_t6.py running the released CLI), verdicts reach MilestoneRecord.exitCriteria as evidence strings naming output hash; nothing under plat/ reads a capture (§17.1 (3); T-V12-28).

Writing rows: plat measure writes per-seed values; plat baselines aggregate (product code run research-side) forms each row's values by §3.5.1's estimator and for distribution rows spreadKS; rows.py adds §13.5 provenance (referenceBuild, capture, script, date), sample block, role from §13.5 or the owning volume; script and capture written as research:-prefixed opaque labels (research:baselines/adapters/mfcg.py) the product never resolves (C2).

The crossing: plat baselines check <file> [--previous] runs on every candidate numbers-only file before commit (baselines.json, ftg-captures.json, ng-counts.json, fm-captures.json, dw-captures.json, vg-seeds.json, a panel's answers.json and key.json after reveal, the corpus's frames.json; BCR-V12-8 adds the new ones to §17.1 (4)); until M1 its twin research/baselines/cross_check.py applies the same rules, M1's first product run re-validates the M-1 file (T-V12-1). Checks (each refused on failure): C1 schema (zod plat.baselines/2, §13.6 (9) types); C2 strings (id, metric, supersedes ^[a-z0-9.:/@+_-]{1,120}$; sample.family, sample.captures[], panel seed labels and reference ids ^[A-Za-z0-9.:/@+_-]{1,120}$; builds ^[A-Za-z0-9._:+-]{1,64}$; dates ISO 8601; capture folder name or research: label; script ^research:[a-z0-9_./-]{1,160}$; any other string field refused); C3 notes (<= 200 chars of letters, digits, spaces, .,;:()-/%±≤≥×, passes the scanner); C4 colours (no six-hex-digit sequence); C5 numbers finite, units in the closed list; C6 metrics exist at the row's metricVersion; C7 samples (registered capture/ family, indices from 0; FTG captures equal plan slots in order; panel FM, DW, VG references the plan's in order); C8 corpus (reference corpus:frame:<id> or corpus:map:<16 hex>; evidence present; a target row is a frame row with frameN >= 20 and evidence surveyed; frame in frames.json by an EARLIER CrossingRecord with equal n and digest; no other corpus string); C9 append-only (no row removed or changed; replaced row kept and named by supersedes); C10 scan (§17.1 (5) scanner over the whole file: 0 hits).

A passing file is committed by the baseline seat (research tier) and countersigned by a checker seat reading only the candidate file, the check output and metrics.json (never captures), appending a CrossingRecord; what never crosses whatever the check says: images, geometry, names, colours, a reference's option names beyond numbers and flags, any corpus string other than our D-2 preset keys (J-V12.2).

Two derived features for sources lacking them (MFCG exports no blocks or lanes; a corpus plate may show buildings only): cluster blocks: footprints whose rings lie within g of each other join one cluster (g = 1.0 m metric, 2% of median footprint short side relative); outline = union closed by dilation then erosion of 3 m (metric) or 10% of that short side (relative); derived street graph: inside the outermost curtain (or built area's outline) the complement of cluster blocks reduced to its straight skeleton (§3.8 kernel), spurs < 8 m (metric) or 40% of median short side (relative) pruned, nodes within 2 m merged; a metric reading blocks or lanes on MFCG reads these and the same metric on our side reads the same derivation from our footprints (never true blocks) (blockc.*, sgd.*); our true blocks and ways feed rows whose reference has them (J-V12.5).

Catalogue conventions: where the base defines a measure the row cites it; m = metric scale needed, f = scale-free; every wall row reads the §2.2 enclosure (item 106): inside the outermost curtain = inside the outermost enclosure; curtain ring's area = enclosure's area; along-curtain distances along built stretches only, never across a closure edge (a condition run's end is no stretch end); a main gate is a gate of class land (a water gate, a harbour-mouth chain included, never counts).

Default rules: absFloor shares, ratios, rank statistics 0.02; angles 1 deg; lengths 2% and areas 5% of reference median; densities 5% of it; counts 0.5; Moran's I and Spearman 0.05; entropies 0.05 bits; timings 5%; sign any for Moran's I, Spearman, z, signed angles, positive otherwise; distribution bins: areas log-spaced 24 bins (blocks 50-50 000 m2; buildings 10-2 000 m2; plots 20-5 000 m2) with underflow and overflow; run lengths 5 m bins to 400 m; NN distances 0.25 m bins to 30 m; widths 0.25 m bins to 30 m; tolerance geo, model, trace, counts 1e-9 relative, render 0.01 absolute, M-1 twin comparison 0.5% relative or one unit of last printed digit; stages: ways S3, S4, S5, S8; walls, towers, gates, castle, closures, enclosures S3-S5; districts and squares S3, S6-S7b; blocks S8-S9; plots S8-S10; buildings S10-S11; water, river, pier S1 and S3; green, field, tree S12-S12a; galleries and chambers the underground stages (II.7); retaining walls S10-S11; raised parts, supports, spans S4-S6 (viaducts S4, elevated roads and aqueducts end of S6).

Metric catalogue rows (street.turn100, street.stepHist, street.entropy50, street.drift600, junction.angles, junction.share4): street.turn100 [geo, m] ways other than alleys resampled at 10 m arc steps; turning = Σ /Δheading/ between steps × 100 ÷ length; per seed the length-weighted median over ways ≥ 50 m  /  ref FTG; PLAT organic presets  /  row §13.5 street turning ;; street.stepHist [geo, m] histogram of /Δheading/ per 10 m step, 1° bins over 0–45° plus overflow; the cliff clause reads it  /  ref FTG (weakness)  /  row street turning ;; street.entropy50 [geo, m] Shannon entropy in bits of the heading change per 50 m window, 5° bins over 0–90°  /  ref FTG (weakness)  /  row street turning ;; street.drift600 [model, m] §4.4's net turn over 600 m of grown streets, organic regimes  /  ref —  /  row growth drift ;; junction.angles [geo, f] nodes of degree ≥ 3 after merging nodes within 2 m; each arm's direction 10 m along it; angles between angularly consecutive arms; per seed median and p5  /  ref NG; FTG  /  row junction arm angles ;; junction.share4 [geo, f] degree-4 nodes ÷ nodes of degree ≥ 3  /  ref NG; FTG  /  row junction arm angles

Metric catalogue rows (street.runs, lots.r4.60, .120, .250, lots.wallAlign, sgd.tShare, sgd.deadEnds, blockc.perHa): street.runs [geo, m] lengths of maximal paths between nodes of degree ≠ 2, per way class; per seed median per class  /  ref FTG  /  row street runs by class ;; lots.r4.60, .120, .250 [geo, m] each building's axis = its longest ring edge's direction; z = e^{4iθ}; for 1 500 buildings sampled by the metric's stream (all if fewer), R4 = /mean z/ over buildings whose centroids lie within r of the sample's centroid, samples with ≥ 5 such buildings; per seed median  /  ref MFCG  /  row MFCG street signature ;; lots.wallAlign [geo, m] buildings inside the outermost curtain, in bands 0–40, 40–100, 100–200 m from it: the angle between the building axis and the nearest curtain segment folded into [0°, 45°]; per band the median and the share ≤ 15°  /  ref MFCG  /  row MFCG street signature ;; sgd.tShare [geo, f] on the derived street graph, degree-3 nodes with two arms within 20° of straight ÷ degree-3 nodes  /  ref MFCG  /  row MFCG street signature ;; sgd.deadEnds [geo, m] degree-1 nodes of the derived street graph per km of its length  /  ref MFCG  /  row MFCG street signature ;; blockc.perHa [geo, m] cluster blocks inside the outermost curtain per walled hectare  /  ref MFCG  /  row MFCG street signature

Estimators: a reference's per-seed statistics s1..sn give spread [a, b] and centre c (median): n = 1 -> a = b = c (single); 2 <= n < 10 -> [min, max] (minmax); n >= 10 -> p10 and p90 by linear interpolation (Hyndman and Fan type 7); with n i.i.d. draws [min, max] covers on average (n - 1)/(n + 1) (0.82 at n = 10), so at ten seeds the two aim at the same interval as §13.5's [p10, p90] (J-V12.3).

Scalar target bands: positive metric: lo = min(a x 0.9, c x 0.85), hi = max(b x 1.1, c x 1.15) (union of §13.5's rule and its single-value +-15%; n = 1 reduces exactly to §13.5's single-value rule); then lo <= c - absFloor and hi >= c + absFloor enforced; sign any: w = max(b - a, absFloor), lo = a - 0.1 w, hi = b + 0.1 w; ours = median of our per-seed statistics; a target row passes when lo <= ours <= hi (J-V12.6).

Distribution target bands: reference seed-to-seed spread = p90 (type 7) of two-sample KS distances over its n(n - 1)/2 seed pairs (n = 2 the one value); ours = median over every (our seed j, reference seed i) pair of KS(tj, si); row passes when ours <= 1.25 x that spread (J-V12.7); at n = 1: ceiling = KS critical value c(0.01) x sqrt((n1 + n2)/(n1 n2)), c(0.01) = 1.628, n1 the one reference seed's element count, n2 our median-sized seed's.

Weakness, descriptive and declared exceptions: a weakness row compares ours (median) with its one-sided bound and margin as §13.5 states; a descriptive row is reported and gates nothing; a row whose band §13.5 or a volume declares as an exception (organic turning's 0.5-1.5 x FTG; V02's chi-square and KS clauses for FM's small sample) carries that band as band.override and the report prints 'declared exception'.

Parity run (plat parity --tier nightly / milestone [--html] [--csv]): 1 load baselines.json; re-run C1, C5, C6, C9 vs last committed hash; select rows whose build equals their reference's pin and metricVersion the registry's; 2 resolve each row's setting: MFCG matched population = the population whose expected non-hinterland building count equals the reference's median building count at that size, round(3.4 x count / (1 - h)) (§12.2's 3.4 persons per building; h the hinterland share of buildings measured on B-CITY-lite at that rung, solved once per rung at each milestone and recorded in the report's setting; J-V12.8); FTG rows the capture's recorded population; NG rows the districts ng-counts.json records from §13.6 (2)'s search; VG and FM rows V07's and V02's settings; 3 generate our towns on bref/<ref>/<rung>/<water>/<i> (20 nightly, 100 milestone) once per preset arm the setting's rows need (reference's own preset for P rows: MFCG or FTG (T23-1), NG (T-V1-31), VG (T-V7-23), FM (fm.* rows, T-V2-31); 'default' for O and C rows); 4 per town measureInputOf and geo metrics; model and trace from bench statistics; render on nightly and milestone tiers only; timing only in §12.1's timing phase; 5 per row per-seed statistics -> ours -> band -> verdict; 6 write the ParityReport (§3.13 canonical form), dashboard, CSV; at a milestone store at plat/goldens/parity/<milestone>.json and name it in MilestoneRecord (§13.3).

Per town: 1 members M = placed uses of the subject's classes; fewer than minMembers (1 pooled, 3 rank) or lacking a required feature -> skipped and counted; 2 eligible sites per scope unit: hardNeeds (plots meeting every hard need of the subject's siting profile, V11 §2.3: the null tests soft pulls, never physical ones), sameSizeClass (plots within the class's template area range), anyPlot; members' own plots eligible; servedShare and nnSameKind at scope town only; 3 S_obs; 4 for k = 1..K (20) per scope unit draw as many eligible plots as members without replacement from testkit stream null/<spec>/<rung>/<water>/<i>/perm, S_k; 5 rank u = (#{S_k < S_obs} + U x (#{S_k = S_obs} + 1)) / (K + 1), U uniform from stream .../tie, S negated when expect lower; uniform on (0,1) under no pull however discrete (§13.2 faithfulness campaign's randomised tie-break; J-V12.12).

Pooled route (shareWithin, downstreamShare, downwindShare, prestigeShare): per scope unit the null count is hypergeometric (m members from E eligible plots, G satisfying the indicator); a town's null the convolution of its units'; the pooled null the convolution over counted towns, computed in integer-indexed doubles in town order with fixed summation order (§3.13); passes when P(pooled count >= observed) <= alpha (0.01; expect lower: <= observed) and where stated the pooled observed share exceeds the pooled null mean share by at least minShift; the headroom lint refuses a nearly-always-true indicator. Rank route: passes when the share of counted towns with u > 0.5 is at least townShare (0.70) and median u >= medianU (0.60); exact p for a holm family = P(Binomial(n, 1/2) >= count of towns with u > 0.5); margin rule: median over towns of S_obs - mean S_k at least the stated value (T71-3's 0.15 of the prime-frontage share, §13.7); holm family (T-V11-12 each shift p < 0.01 Holm-corrected) runs Holm's step-down over its specs' p-values.
